ResStock assigns air infiltration rates (ACH50) to each simulated dwelling from the LBNL
Residential Diagnostics Database (ResDB). An overestimate of infiltration directly inflates
both heating and cooling loads — but by different amounts, because infiltration is a larger
fraction of the heating load than the cooling load.

This notebook investigates whether a systematic ACH50 overestimate could explain the
varied overstatement of heating and cooling loads that we observe when comparing ResStock
to RECS 2020. It fits a weighted linear regression within each heating-type group for
electric heating, electric cooling, and gas heating end-uses, uses the regression to
simulate per-building load corrections under a range of ACH50 reductions, and evaluates
how close the corrected electric total gets to the BGE test-year kWh. The same correction
is applied to natural gas heating loads for consistency.

```{python}
#| label: setup

    geom_smooth,
```


## RECS 2020 microdata

We load the EIA [Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) 2020](https://www.eia.gov/consumption/residential/data/2020/)
microdata directly, rather than hardcoding benchmark values from a prior analysis. This
lets us compute kWh/sqft benchmarks from the raw data, verify them in-notebook, and
explore additional metrics like cooling intensity per *cooled* square footage.

```{python}
#| label: load-recs

RECS_PATH = Path("../cache/recs2020_public_v7.csv")

recs_all = pl.read_csv(RECS_PATH, infer_schema_length=20000)
recs_md = recs_all.filter(pl.col("state_postal") == STATE_UPPER)
print(f"RECS 2020 Maryland respondents: {len(recs_md)}")
```

### Classify RECS homes by heating type

We follow the RECS equipment code classification documented in
`bge_resstock_recs_load_validation.md`: heat pumps are EQUIPM ∈ {4, 13}, electric
resistance is EQUIPM ∈ {3, 5, 10} with FUELHEAT = 5 (electricity), and non-electric-heat
homes have FUELHEAT ≠ 5.

```{python}
#| label: recs-classify

recs_md = recs_md.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("EQUIPM").is_in([4, 13]))
    .then(pl.lit("Heat Pump"))
    .when(pl.col("EQUIPM").is_in([3, 5, 10]) & (pl.col("FUELHEAT") == 5))
    .then(pl.lit("Resistance"))
    .when(pl.col("FUELHEAT") != 5)
    .then(pl.lit("Non-electric"))
    .otherwise(pl.lit("Other"))
    .alias("recs_group"),
)

# Verify: counts and weighted population by group
for g in ["Resistance", "Heat Pump", "Non-electric", "Other"]:
    sub = recs_md.filter(pl.col("recs_group") == g)
    wt = sub["NWEIGHT"].sum()
    print(f"  {g:<20s}  n={len(sub):>4d}   wtd={wt/1e6:.2f}M")
```

### Compute RECS benchmarks

We compute weighted-average kWh per square foot for each heating-type group and end-use.
For electric heating, all homes in each group contribute (they all have the relevant
equipment). For electric cooling, we restrict to homes **with cooling equipment**
(`ACEQUIPM_PUB > 0`), since homes without AC have zero cooling kWh by definition —
including them would dilute the intensity benchmark. For gas heating, we use the
space-heating-specific variable `CUFEETNGSPH` (CCF ≈ therms) on non-electric homes with
gas heating (`CUFEETNGSPH > 0`).

The method is "weighted mean of per-building ratios": $\sum w_i \cdot (\text{kWh}_i /
\text{sqft}_i) \;/\; \sum w_i$, which gives each household equal influence regardless of
size.

```{python}
#| label: recs-benchmarks

recs_nw = recs_md["NWEIGHT"].to_numpy().astype(float)
recs_sqft = recs_md["TOTSQFT_EN"].to_numpy().astype(float)
recs_csqft = recs_md["TOTCSQFT"].to_numpy().astype(float)
recs_hsqft = recs_md["TOTHSQFT"].to_numpy().astype(float)
recs_kwhsph = recs_md["KWHSPH"].to_numpy().astype(float)
recs_kwhcol = recs_md["KWHCOL"].to_numpy().astype(float)
recs_gas_sph = recs_md["CUFEETNGSPH"].to_numpy().astype(float)
recs_acequipm = recs_md["ACEQUIPM_PUB"].to_numpy().astype(int)
recs_group_arr = recs_md["recs_group"].to_list()

def recs_group_mask(group: str) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array([g == group for g in recs_group_arr])

RECS_BENCHMARKS: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}

print("RECS benchmarks using TOTSQFT_EN (total floor area) as denominator:")
print(f"{'Group':<20s}  {'End-use':<15s}  {'kWh/sqft':>10s}  {'N':>5s}  {'Notes'}")
print("-" * 75)

for g in ["Resistance", "Heat Pump", "Non-electric"]:
    mask = recs_group_mask(g)
    w = recs_nw[mask]
    sqft = recs_sqft[mask]

    # Electric heating: all homes in group
    heat = recs_kwhsph[mask]
    heat_psf = (w * heat / sqft).sum() / w.sum()
    RECS_BENCHMARKS[(g, "Elec heating")] = heat_psf
    print(f"{g:<20s}  {'Elec heating':<15s}  {heat_psf:>10.2f}  {mask.sum():>5d}  all homes in group")

    # Electric cooling: homes with AC only (ACEQUIPM_PUB > 0)
    has_ac = recs_acequipm[mask] > 0
    cool = recs_kwhcol[mask]
    cool_psf = (w[has_ac] * cool[has_ac] / sqft[has_ac]).sum() / w[has_ac].sum()
    RECS_BENCHMARKS[(g, "Elec cooling")] = cool_psf
    print(f"{g:<20s}  {'Elec cooling':<15s}  {cool_psf:>10.2f}  {has_ac.sum():>5d}  AC owners only")

# Gas heating: non-electric homes with gas space heating
ne_mask = recs_group_mask("Non-electric")
has_gas = recs_gas_sph[ne_mask] > 0
w_ne = recs_nw[ne_mask]
sqft_ne = recs_sqft[ne_mask]
gas = recs_gas_sph[ne_mask]
gas_therms_psf = (w_ne[has_gas] * gas[has_gas] / sqft_ne[has_gas]).sum() / w_ne[has_gas].sum()
gas_kwh_psf = gas_therms_psf * 29.3
RECS_BENCHMARKS[("Non-electric", "Gas heating")] = gas_kwh_psf
print(f"{'Non-electric':<20s}  {'Gas heating':<15s}  {gas_kwh_psf:>10.2f}  {has_gas.sum():>5d}  gas users, {gas_therms_psf:.3f} therms/sqft × 29.3")

# --- Adjusted benchmarks: conditioned sqft as denominator ---
# Heating uses TOTHSQFT; cooling uses TOTCSQFT.  These are the physically
# meaningful denominators because RECS homes often condition only part of
# their floor area, while ResStock assumes whole-house conditioning.
RECS_BENCHMARKS_ADJUSTED: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}

print()
print("RECS benchmarks using conditioned sqft (TOTHSQFT / TOTCSQFT) as denominator:")
print(f"{'Group':<20s}  {'End-use':<15s}  {'kWh/cond.sqft':>14s}  {'N':>5s}  {'Notes'}")
print("-" * 80)

for g in ["Resistance", "Heat Pump", "Non-electric"]:
    mask = recs_group_mask(g)
    w = recs_nw[mask]
    hsqft = recs_hsqft[mask]

    # Electric heating: homes with heated sqft > 0
    heat = recs_kwhsph[mask]
    has_h = hsqft > 0
    heat_adj = (w[has_h] * heat[has_h] / hsqft[has_h]).sum() / w[has_h].sum()
    RECS_BENCHMARKS_ADJUSTED[(g, "Elec heating")] = heat_adj
    print(f"{g:<20s}  {'Elec heating':<15s}  {heat_adj:>14.2f}  {has_h.sum():>5d}  homes w/ TOTHSQFT > 0")

    # Electric cooling: AC owners with cooled sqft > 0
    has_ac = recs_acequipm[mask] > 0
    csqft = recs_csqft[mask]
    cool = recs_kwhcol[mask]
    ac_and_csqft = has_ac & (csqft > 0)
    cool_adj = (w[ac_and_csqft] * cool[ac_and_csqft] / csqft[ac_and_csqft]).sum() / w[ac_and_csqft].sum()
    RECS_BENCHMARKS_ADJUSTED[(g, "Elec cooling")] = cool_adj
    print(f"{g:<20s}  {'Elec cooling':<15s}  {cool_adj:>14.2f}  {ac_and_csqft.sum():>5d}  AC + TOTCSQFT > 0")

# Gas heating: non-electric homes with gas + heated sqft > 0
ne_hsqft = recs_hsqft[ne_mask]
has_gas_h = has_gas & (ne_hsqft > 0)
gas_therms_adj = (w_ne[has_gas_h] * gas[has_gas_h] / ne_hsqft[has_gas_h]).sum() / w_ne[has_gas_h].sum()
gas_kwh_adj = gas_therms_adj * 29.3
RECS_BENCHMARKS_ADJUSTED[("Non-electric", "Gas heating")] = gas_kwh_adj
print(f"{'Non-electric':<20s}  {'Gas heating':<15s}  {gas_kwh_adj:>14.2f}  {has_gas_h.sum():>5d}  gas + TOTHSQFT > 0, {gas_therms_adj:.3f} therms/sqft × 29.3")

# --- Side-by-side summary ---
print()
print(f"{'Group':<20s}  {'End-use':<15s}  {'kWh/total sqft':>15s}  {'kWh/cond. sqft':>15s}  {'Δ%':>6s}")
print("-" * 80)
for key in RECS_BENCHMARKS:
    orig = RECS_BENCHMARKS[key]
    adj = RECS_BENCHMARKS_ADJUSTED[key]
    g, eu = key
    pct_diff = (adj - orig) / orig * 100
    print(f"{g:<20s}  {eu:<15s}  {orig:>15.2f}  {adj:>15.2f}  {pct_diff:>+5.0f}%")

print()
print("The adjusted benchmarks are higher because the denominator (conditioned area)")
print("is smaller than total floor area. The Δ% reflects the partial-conditioning")
print("gap that ResStock's whole-house assumption obscures.")
```

### Distribution of RECS kWh/sqft by heating type

The weighted means above are point estimates. With sample sizes of 59–217 per group, the
underlying distributions matter — a wide spread or heavy tails would weaken the benchmark,
while a tight distribution would strengthen it. We report the full range (min–max),
interquartile range (P25–P75), weighted standard deviation, and the standard error of the
weighted mean for each end-use × group combination.

```{python}
#| label: recs-distribution

def weighted_stats(values: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """Compute weighted mean, std, SE, and percentiles."""
    w_sum = weights.sum()
    w_mean = (weights * values).sum() / w_sum
    w_var = (weights * (values - w_mean) ** 2).sum() / w_sum
    w_std = np.sqrt(w_var)
    n_eff = w_sum**2 / (weights**2).sum()
    w_se = w_std / np.sqrt(n_eff)
    sorted_idx = np.argsort(values)
    sorted_vals = values[sorted_idx]
    sorted_wts = weights[sorted_idx]
    cum_wt = np.cumsum(sorted_wts)
    cum_wt_norm = cum_wt / cum_wt[-1]
    p25 = sorted_vals[np.searchsorted(cum_wt_norm, 0.25)]
    p50 = sorted_vals[np.searchsorted(cum_wt_norm, 0.50)]
    p75 = sorted_vals[np.searchsorted(cum_wt_norm, 0.75)]
    return {
        "mean": w_mean, "std": w_std, "se": w_se, "n_eff": n_eff,
        "min": values.min(), "p25": p25, "p50": p50, "p75": p75, "max": values.max(),
        "n": len(values),
    }

print("RECS 2020 Maryland — kWh/sqft distribution by heating type and end-use")
print()
print(f"{'Group':<16s}  {'End-use':<13s}  {'N':>4s}  {'Mean':>6s}  {'SE':>6s}  "
      f"{'Std':>6s}  {'Min':>6s}  {'P25':>6s}  {'P50':>6s}  {'P75':>6s}  {'Max':>6s}")
print("-" * 105)

for g in ["Resistance", "Heat Pump", "Non-electric"]:
    mask = recs_group_mask(g)
    w = recs_nw[mask]
    sqft = recs_sqft[mask]

    # Electric heating (all homes in group)
    heat_psf = recs_kwhsph[mask] / sqft
    s = weighted_stats(heat_psf, w)
    print(f"{g:<16s}  {'Elec heating':<13s}  {s['n']:>4d}  {s['mean']:>6.2f}  {s['se']:>6.2f}  "
          f"{s['std']:>6.2f}  {s['min']:>6.2f}  {s['p25']:>6.2f}  {s['p50']:>6.2f}  {s['p75']:>6.2f}  {s['max']:>6.2f}")

    # Electric cooling (AC owners only)
    has_ac = recs_acequipm[mask] > 0
    if has_ac.sum() > 0:
        cool_psf = recs_kwhcol[mask][has_ac] / sqft[has_ac]
        s = weighted_stats(cool_psf, w[has_ac])
        print(f"{g:<16s}  {'Elec cooling':<13s}  {s['n']:>4d}  {s['mean']:>6.2f}  {s['se']:>6.2f}  "
              f"{s['std']:>6.2f}  {s['min']:>6.2f}  {s['p25']:>6.2f}  {s['p50']:>6.2f}  {s['p75']:>6.2f}  {s['max']:>6.2f}")

    # Gas heating (non-electric, gas users only) — in therms/sqft
    if g == "Non-electric":
        has_gas_g = recs_gas_sph[mask] > 0
        if has_gas_g.sum() > 0:
            gas_psf = recs_gas_sph[mask][has_gas_g] / sqft[has_gas_g]
            s = weighted_stats(gas_psf, w[has_gas_g])
            print(f"{g:<16s}  {'Gas htg thm':<13s}  {s['n']:>4d}  {s['mean']:>6.3f}  {s['se']:>6.3f}  "
                  f"{s['std']:>6.3f}  {s['min']:>6.3f}  {s['p25']:>6.3f}  {s['p50']:>6.3f}  {s['p75']:>6.3f}  {s['max']:>6.3f}")
            print(f"{'':>16s}  {'  (×29.3 kWh)':<13s}  {'':>4s}  {s['mean']*29.3:>6.2f}  {s['se']*29.3:>6.2f}  "
                  f"{s['std']*29.3:>6.2f}  {s['min']*29.3:>6.2f}  {s['p25']*29.3:>6.2f}  {s['p50']*29.3:>6.2f}  {s['p75']*29.3:>6.2f}  {s['max']*29.3:>6.2f}")

    print()
```

### Bootstrap confidence intervals

The weighted means above are point estimates from 59–217 RECS respondents per group. To
assess how much sampling variability these estimates carry, we compute confidence intervals
using two complementary methods:

1. **Jackknife replicate weights (JK1)**: RECS 2020 provides 60 replicate weights
   (`NWEIGHT1`–`NWEIGHT60`) designed for variance estimation under the complex survey design.
   The JK1 variance is $\text{Var} = \frac{59}{60} \sum_{r=1}^{60} (\hat\theta_r - \hat\theta_0)^2$,
   where $\hat\theta_0$ is the full-sample estimate and $\hat\theta_r$ uses replicate weight $r$.
   This is EIA's recommended approach and correctly accounts for stratification and clustering.

2. **Case-resample bootstrap** (2,000 resamples): For visualization, we also draw bootstrap
   samples with replacement from the respondents within each group, using the original
   `NWEIGHT` in the weighted-mean calculation. This gives a richer distribution to plot as a
   histogram.

```{python}
#| label: recs-bootstrap

N_REPS = 60
JK_SCALE = (N_REPS - 1) / N_REPS  # 59/60
N_BOOT = 2000
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

rep_weight_cols = [f"NWEIGHT{r}" for r in range(1, N_REPS + 1)]
rep_weights = recs_md.select(rep_weight_cols).to_numpy().astype(float)

def weighted_mean_ratio(values: np.ndarray, denoms: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Weighted mean of per-building ratios: sum(w * v/d) / sum(w)."""
    return (weights * values / denoms).sum() / weights.sum()

# Define the 6 benchmarks: (label, group_mask_indices, numerator, denominator, weights, rep_weights)
benchmark_specs: list[dict] = []

for g in ["Resistance", "Heat Pump"]:
    mask = recs_group_mask(g)
    benchmark_specs.append({
        "label": f"{g}, Elec heating",
        "values": recs_kwhsph[mask],
        "denoms": recs_sqft[mask],
        "base_w": recs_nw[mask],
        "rep_w": rep_weights[mask],
    })
    ac_sub = recs_acequipm[mask] > 0
    benchmark_specs.append({
        "label": f"{g}, Elec cooling",
        "values": recs_kwhcol[mask][ac_sub],
        "denoms": recs_sqft[mask][ac_sub],
        "base_w": recs_nw[mask][ac_sub],
        "rep_w": rep_weights[mask][ac_sub],
    })

ne_mask = recs_group_mask("Non-electric")
ne_ac = recs_acequipm[ne_mask] > 0
benchmark_specs.append({
    "label": "Non-electric, Elec cooling",
    "values": recs_kwhcol[ne_mask][ne_ac],
    "denoms": recs_sqft[ne_mask][ne_ac],
    "base_w": recs_nw[ne_mask][ne_ac],
    "rep_w": rep_weights[ne_mask][ne_ac],
})
ne_gas = recs_gas_sph[ne_mask] > 0
benchmark_specs.append({
    "label": "Non-electric, Gas heating",
    "values": recs_gas_sph[ne_mask][ne_gas] * 29.3,
    "denoms": recs_sqft[ne_mask][ne_gas],
    "base_w": recs_nw[ne_mask][ne_gas],
    "rep_w": rep_weights[ne_mask][ne_gas],
})

# Compute JK variance and bootstrap distribution for each benchmark
boot_rows: list[dict] = []
summary_rows: list[dict] = []

for spec in benchmark_specs:
    v, d, bw, rw = spec["values"], spec["denoms"], spec["base_w"], spec["rep_w"]
    n = len(v)
    theta_0 = weighted_mean_ratio(v, d, bw)

    # Jackknife replicate estimates
    theta_r = np.array([weighted_mean_ratio(v, d, rw[:, r]) for r in range(N_REPS)])
    jk_var = JK_SCALE * np.sum((theta_r - theta_0) ** 2)
    jk_se = np.sqrt(jk_var)

    # Case-resample bootstrap
    boot_est = np.empty(N_BOOT)
    for b in range(N_BOOT):
        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
        boot_est[b] = weighted_mean_ratio(v[idx], d[idx], bw[idx])

    for val in boot_est:
        boot_rows.append({"benchmark": spec["label"], "boot_value": val})

    summary_rows.append({
        "benchmark": spec["label"],
        "n": n,
        "point_est": round(theta_0, 3),
        "jk_se": round(jk_se, 3),
        "jk_ci_lo": round(theta_0 - 1.96 * jk_se, 3),
        "jk_ci_hi": round(theta_0 + 1.96 * jk_se, 3),
        "ci_width_pct": round((2 * 1.96 * jk_se) / theta_0 * 100, 1),
    })

boot_df = pl.DataFrame(boot_rows)
summary_df = pl.DataFrame(summary_rows)

# Panel ordering for facet_wrap
panel_order = [s["label"] for s in benchmark_specs]
boot_df = boot_df.with_columns(pl.col("benchmark").cast(pl.Enum(panel_order)))

# Annotation dataframes for vertical lines
point_line_df = pl.DataFrame([
    {"benchmark": r["benchmark"], "x": r["point_est"]} for r in summary_rows
]).with_columns(pl.col("benchmark").cast(pl.Enum(panel_order)))

ci_lo_df = pl.DataFrame([
    {"benchmark": r["benchmark"], "x": r["jk_ci_lo"]} for r in summary_rows
]).with_columns(pl.col("benchmark").cast(pl.Enum(panel_order)))

ci_hi_df = pl.DataFrame([
    {"benchmark": r["benchmark"], "x": r["jk_ci_hi"]} for r in summary_rows
]).with_columns(pl.col("benchmark").cast(pl.Enum(panel_order)))

p = (
    ggplot(boot_df, aes(x="boot_value"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=40, fill=SB_COLORS["sky"], alpha=0.7, color="white")
    + geom_vline(point_line_df, aes(xintercept="x"), color=SB_COLORS["midnight"], size=1.2)
    + geom_vline(ci_lo_df, aes(xintercept="x"), color=SB_COLORS["carrot"], linetype="dashed", size=0.8)
    + geom_vline(ci_hi_df, aes(xintercept="x"), color=SB_COLORS["carrot"], linetype="dashed", size=0.8)
    + facet_wrap("benchmark", scales="free", ncol=3)
    + labs(
        title="Bootstrap distributions of RECS 2020 Maryland kWh/sqft benchmarks",
        subtitle="Solid line = point estimate; dashed lines = JK-based 95% CI",
        x="kWh / sqft",
        y="Count (2,000 bootstrap resamples)",
    )
    + theme_switchbox()
    + theme(figure_size=(10.5, 6.5))
)
p
```

The table below shows the point estimate, jackknife standard error, and 95% CI for each
benchmark. The CI width as a percentage of the point estimate indicates how precisely each
benchmark is measured — wider CIs warrant more caution when using the benchmark to
evaluate ResStock accuracy.

```{python}
#| label: recs-bootstrap-summary

summary_df
```

The heating benchmarks carry wider relative CIs (31–37%) than the cooling benchmarks
(19–27%), driven by larger variance in heating intensity across homes and smaller sample
sizes (69–73 vs. 59–203). The gas heating benchmark, despite its larger absolute CI
width, is reasonably precise relative to its magnitude (20%). The non-electric cooling
benchmark is the tightest (19% CI width), benefiting from the largest sample (n=203).

Even at their widest, these CIs are narrow enough that the qualitative finding —
ResStock substantially overstates heating loads relative to RECS — holds across the
entire confidence range. The smallest ResStock-vs-RECS gap (resistance electric heating)
still exceeds the upper bound of the RECS CI.

### Cooling intensity: total sqft vs cooled sqft

ResStock assumes whole-house cooling for every home with AC. But RECS reports both total
floor area (`TOTSQFT_EN`) and cooled floor area (`TOTCSQFT`), revealing that many homes
cool only a portion of their space. The weighted-average cooled fraction across Maryland
homes with AC is roughly 80–90% depending on heating type — meaning ResStock's
whole-house assumption inflates the effective cooling area by 10–20%.

This matters for benchmarking: cooling kWh per *cooled* square foot is the more
physically meaningful metric for comparing against ResStock's simulated cooling loads.

```{python}
#| label: recs-cooling-sqft

# Filter to AC owners (ACEQUIPM_PUB > 0), consistent with the benchmarks above.
# Homes without AC have zero cooling kWh; including them dilutes the intensity.
print(f"{'Group':<20s}  {'kWh/TOTSQFT':>12s}  {'kWh/TOTCSQFT':>14s}  {'Cooled frac':>12s}  {'N (AC owners)':>14s}")
print("-" * 80)

RECS_COOLING_PER_COOLED_SQFT: dict[str, float] = {}

for g in ["Resistance", "Heat Pump", "Non-electric", "All homes"]:
    if g == "All homes":
        mask = np.ones(len(recs_nw), dtype=bool)
    else:
        mask = recs_group_mask(g)

    # Restrict to AC owners
    has_ac = recs_acequipm[mask] > 0
    w = recs_nw[mask][has_ac]
    sqft = recs_sqft[mask][has_ac]
    csqft = recs_csqft[mask][has_ac]
    cool = recs_kwhcol[mask][has_ac]
    has_c = csqft > 0

    cool_per_totsqft = (w * cool / sqft).sum() / w.sum()
    cool_per_csqft = (w[has_c] * cool[has_c] / csqft[has_c]).sum() / w[has_c].sum() if has_c.sum() > 0 else float("nan")
    cooled_frac = (w * np.where(sqft > 0, csqft / sqft, 0)).sum() / w.sum()

    RECS_COOLING_PER_COOLED_SQFT[g] = cool_per_csqft

    print(f"{g:<20s}  {cool_per_totsqft:>12.2f}  {cool_per_csqft:>14.2f}  {cooled_frac:>11.1%}  {has_ac.sum():>5d}/{mask.sum():>3d}")

print()
print("Both columns are restricted to AC owners, matching the RECS_BENCHMARKS filter.")
print("'kWh/TOTSQFT' matches the benchmark used for gap-closing comparisons above.")
print("'kWh/TOTCSQFT' uses cooled sqft as the denominator — the physically meaningful")
print("intensity for comparing against ResStock, which assumes whole-house cooling.")
```

### Heating intensity: total sqft vs heated sqft

The same partial-conditioning issue applies to heating. RECS reports heated floor area
(`TOTHSQFT`) alongside total floor area (`TOTSQFT_EN`). Many homes — especially older
ones — don't heat their entire floor area (basements, attics, spare rooms). ResStock
assumes whole-house heating, so its simulated heating loads are spread over the full
floor area. The ratio of `TOTHSQFT / TOTSQFT_EN` tells us how large the
partial-heating gap is in RECS.

```{python}
#| label: recs-heating-sqft

print(f"{'Group':<20s}  {'kWh/TOTSQFT':>12s}  {'kWh/TOTHSQFT':>14s}  {'Heated frac':>12s}  {'N':>14s}")
print("-" * 80)

RECS_HEATING_PER_HEATED_SQFT: dict[str, float] = {}

# Electric heating by group
for g in ["Resistance", "Heat Pump", "Non-electric", "All homes"]:
    if g == "All homes":
        mask = np.ones(len(recs_nw), dtype=bool)
    else:
        mask = recs_group_mask(g)

    w = recs_nw[mask]
    sqft = recs_sqft[mask]
    hsqft = recs_hsqft[mask]
    heat = recs_kwhsph[mask]
    has_h = hsqft > 0

    heat_per_totsqft = (w * heat / sqft).sum() / w.sum()
    heat_per_hsqft = (w[has_h] * heat[has_h] / hsqft[has_h]).sum() / w[has_h].sum() if has_h.sum() > 0 else float("nan")
    heated_frac = (w * np.where(sqft > 0, hsqft / sqft, 0)).sum() / w.sum()

    RECS_HEATING_PER_HEATED_SQFT[g] = heat_per_hsqft

    print(f"{g:<20s}  {heat_per_totsqft:>12.2f}  {heat_per_hsqft:>14.2f}  {heated_frac:>11.1%}  {has_h.sum():>5d}/{mask.sum():>3d}")

# Gas heating for non-electric homes
print()
print("Gas heating (non-electric homes with CUFEETNGSPH > 0):")
print(f"{'':20s}  {'thm/TOTSQFT':>12s}  {'thm/TOTHSQFT':>14s}  {'kWh-eq/TOTHSQFT':>16s}  {'Heated frac':>12s}  {'N':>5s}")
print("-" * 90)

ne_mask = recs_group_mask("Non-electric")
w_ne = recs_nw[ne_mask]
sqft_ne = recs_sqft[ne_mask]
hsqft_ne = recs_hsqft[ne_mask]
gas = recs_gas_sph[ne_mask]
has_gas_h = (gas > 0) & (hsqft_ne > 0)
has_gas_any = gas > 0

gas_per_totsqft = (w_ne[has_gas_any] * gas[has_gas_any] / sqft_ne[has_gas_any]).sum() / w_ne[has_gas_any].sum()
gas_per_hsqft = (w_ne[has_gas_h] * gas[has_gas_h] / hsqft_ne[has_gas_h]).sum() / w_ne[has_gas_h].sum()
heated_frac_gas = (w_ne[has_gas_any] * np.where(sqft_ne[has_gas_any] > 0, hsqft_ne[has_gas_any] / sqft_ne[has_gas_any], 0)).sum() / w_ne[has_gas_any].sum()

print(f"{'Non-electric':<20s}  {gas_per_totsqft:>12.3f}  {gas_per_hsqft:>14.3f}  {gas_per_hsqft * 29.3:>16.2f}  {heated_frac_gas:>11.1%}  {has_gas_h.sum():>5d}")

print()
print("Heated fractions are generally higher than cooled fractions — most homes heat")
print("more of their space than they cool. But the gap is still meaningful: ~90% heated")
print("vs ~80-90% cooled, translating to a 5-15% increase in intensity per conditioned sqft.")
```

## Load data

We need three datasets: ResStock metadata (for `in.infiltration`, `in.sqft`, and heating
type), utility assignments (to filter to BGE), and annual load curves (for end-use kWh and
sample weights). We use `grid_cons = max(total - abs(pv), 0)` for the total kWh, matching
the billing basis in CAIRO and the `build_rate_case_test_year.py` pipeline. This is what
flows through the meter; it differs from `out.electricity.total` for buildings with PV.

```{python}
#| label: load-data

meta = pl.read_parquet(META_PATH)
ua = pl.read_parquet(UA_PATH)
annual = pl.read_parquet(ANNUAL_PATH)

bge_ids = ua.filter(pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == "bge")["bldg_id"].to_list()

print(f"Total MD buildings: {len(meta):,}")
print(f"BGE buildings:      {len(bge_ids):,}")
```

### Join and classify

```{python}
#| label: join-classify

HEATING_E_COLS = [
    "out.electricity.heating.energy_consumption.kwh",
    "out.electricity.heating_fans_pumps.energy_consumption.kwh",
    "out.electricity.heating_hp_bkup.energy_consumption.kwh",
    "out.electricity.heating_hp_bkup_fa.energy_consumption.kwh",
]
COOLING_E_COLS = [
    "out.electricity.cooling.energy_consumption.kwh",
    "out.electricity.cooling_fans_pumps.energy_consumption.kwh",
]
GAS_HEATING_COLS = [
    "out.natural_gas.heating.energy_consumption.kwh",
    "out.natural_gas.heating_hp_bkup.energy_consumption.kwh",
]

ELEC_TOTAL_COL = "out.electricity.total.energy_consumption.kwh"
ELEC_PV_COL = "out.electricity.pv.energy_consumption.kwh"

select_cols = (
    ["bldg_id", "weight", ELEC_TOTAL_COL, ELEC_PV_COL,
     "out.natural_gas.total.energy_consumption.kwh"]
    + HEATING_E_COLS + COOLING_E_COLS + GAS_HEATING_COLS
)

bge = (
    meta
    .filter(pl.col("bldg_id").is_in(bge_ids))
    .join(annual.select(select_cols), on="bldg_id")
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("in.infiltration").str.replace(" ACH50", "").cast(pl.Int32).alias("ach50"),
        pl.col("in.sqft").cast(pl.Float64).alias("sqft"),
        sum(pl.col(c) for c in HEATING_E_COLS).alias("elec_heating_kwh"),
        sum(pl.col(c) for c in COOLING_E_COLS).alias("elec_cooling_kwh"),
        sum(pl.col(c) for c in GAS_HEATING_COLS).alias("gas_heating_kwh"),
        # grid_cons = max(total - abs(pv), 0) — matches CAIRO billing basis
        (pl.col(ELEC_TOTAL_COL) - pl.col(ELEC_PV_COL).abs()).clip(lower_bound=0.0).alias("grid_cons_kwh"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(~pl.col("heats_with_electricity"))
        .then(pl.lit("Non-electric"))
        .when(pl.col("postprocess_group.has_hp"))
        .then(pl.lit("Heat Pump"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("Resistance"))
        .alias("group"),
        (pl.col("elec_heating_kwh") / pl.col("sqft")).alias("heat_per_sqft"),
        (pl.col("elec_cooling_kwh") / pl.col("sqft")).alias("cool_per_sqft"),
        (pl.col("gas_heating_kwh") / pl.col("sqft")).alias("gas_heat_per_sqft"),
    )
)

print(f"BGE buildings loaded: {len(bge):,}")
print(f"Weighted customers:   {bge['weight'].sum():,.0f}")
```

Let's take a quick look at the key columns:

```{python}
bge.select(

    "elec_heating_kwh", "elec_cooling_kwh", "gas_heating_kwh",

).head(10)
```

## ACH50 distribution

ResStock assigns ACH50 values from discrete bins (1, 2, 3, ... 50 ACH50). Published
benchmarks for existing U.S. housing suggest a national median around 12 ACH50 (LBNL
ResDB, Chan et al. 2013, 134k homes), and field practitioners report most existing homes
in the Mid-Atlantic testing at 6–12 ACH50, with values above 15 being unusual.

```{python}
#| label: ach50-distribution

w = bge["weight"].to_numpy().astype(float)
ach = bge["ach50"].to_numpy().astype(float)

wtd_mean = (ach * w).sum() / w.sum()

sorted_idx = np.argsort(ach)
cum_w = np.cumsum(w[sorted_idx]) / w.sum()
p50_idx = np.searchsorted(cum_w, 0.50)
wtd_median = ach[sorted_idx[p50_idx]]

print(f"Weighted mean ACH50:   {wtd_mean:.1f}")
print(f"Weighted median ACH50: {wtd_median:.0f}")
```

## Relationship between ACH50 and loads

The physical model: total heating (or cooling) load is the sum of an infiltration-driven
component and everything else (conduction through the shell, solar gains, internal gains).
Only the infiltration term is proportional to ACH50. So the linear model

$$\text{kWh/sqft} = a + b \times \text{ACH50}$$

has a physical interpretation: the intercept $a$ captures the ACH50-independent base load,
while the slope $b$ captures the marginal kWh/sqft per unit of ACH50. The infiltration
fraction at any ACH50 level is $b \times \text{ACH50} / (a + b \times \text{ACH50})$.

### Weighted linear regression

We now fit the linear model within each group/end-use combination using weighted least
squares. The key outputs are the slope, intercept, and the implied **infiltration fraction**
at the mean ACH50 level.

```{python}
#| label: regression

def weighted_linreg(
    x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, w: np.ndarray
) -> dict:
    """Weighted linear regression y = a + b*x. Returns dict with a, b, r2."""
    sw = w.sum()
    sx = (w * x).sum() / sw
    sy = (w * y).sum() / sw
    sxx = (w * x * x).sum() / sw - sx * sx
    sxy = (w * x * y).sum() / sw - sx * sy
    syy = (w * y * y).sum() / sw - sy * sy

    b = sxy / sxx
    a = sy - b * sx
    r2 = (sxy**2) / (sxx * syy) if syy > 0 else 0.0
    return {"intercept": a, "slope": b, "r2": r2}


ENDUSES = [
    ("Elec heating", "heat_per_sqft", "elec_heating_kwh"),
    ("Elec cooling", "cool_per_sqft", "elec_cooling_kwh"),
    ("Gas heating", "gas_heat_per_sqft", "gas_heating_kwh"),
]

GROUPS = ["Resistance", "Heat Pump", "Non-electric"]

results = []
for g in GROUPS:
    sub = bge.filter(pl.col("group") == g)
    ach_arr = sub["ach50"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    w_arr = sub["weight"].to_numpy().astype(float)

    for enduse_label, per_sqft_col, _raw_col in ENDUSES:
        vals = sub[per_sqft_col].to_numpy()
        mask = (vals > 0) & np.isfinite(vals) & (w_arr > 0)
        if mask.sum() < 10:
            continue

        reg = weighted_linreg(ach_arr[mask], vals[mask], w_arr[mask])
        mean_ach = (ach_arr[mask] * w_arr[mask]).sum() / w_arr[mask].sum()
        total_at_mean = reg["intercept"] + reg["slope"] * mean_ach
        infilt_frac = reg["slope"] * mean_ach / total_at_mean if total_at_mean > 0 else 0

        results.append({
            "group": g,
            "enduse": enduse_label,
            "intercept": reg["intercept"],
            "slope": reg["slope"],
            "r2": reg["r2"],
            "mean_ach50": mean_ach,
            "infilt_fraction": infilt_frac,
            "n": int(mask.sum()),
        })

reg_df = pl.DataFrame(results)
```

```{python}
#| label: show-regression

reg_df.select(
    "group", "enduse",
    pl.col("intercept").round(3),
    pl.col("slope").round(4),
    pl.col("r2").round(3),
    pl.col("mean_ach50").round(1),
    (pl.col("infilt_fraction") * 100).round(0).alias("infilt_%"),
    "n",
)
```

At the mean ACH50 of ~20, infiltration accounts for roughly **61–65% of the heating load**
but only **21–33% of the cooling load**. This is physically consistent: heating losses are
dominated by the building envelope (conduction + infiltration), while cooling loads have
large solar gain and internal gain components that do not depend on ACH50.

Note that the slopes are fitted _separately within each heating-type group_, so they
implicitly capture each system's efficiency (COP). The electric heating slope for heat pump
homes (~0.13 kWh/sqft per ACH50) is roughly half that of resistance homes (~0.24), implying
an effective heating-season COP of ~1.8 — consistent with cold-climate ASHP performance.
The gas heating slope (~0.33 kWh/sqft per ACH50) reflects gas furnace efficiency (~80–95%).
No additional COP adjustment is needed.

## Simulated ACH50 correction

We now apply a uniform percentage reduction to every building's ACH50 and use the linear
model to predict what its heating and cooling loads would be at the reduced ACH50. Electric
non-heating, non-cooling loads are left unchanged. Gas non-heating loads are also left
unchanged.

For a building _i_ in group _g_ with end-use column _e_:

$$\text{corrected}_{i,e} = \max\!\Big(0,\; \text{original}_{i,e} - b_{g,e} \times \text{sqft}_i \times \text{ACH50}_i \times \delta\Big)$$

where $b_{g,e}$ is the regression slope for that group/end-use and $\delta$ is the fractional
ACH50 reduction.

```{python}
#| label: correction-sweep

# Build a lookup of slopes by (group, enduse)
slope_lookup: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}
for row in reg_df.iter_rows(named=True):
    slope_lookup[(row["group"], row["enduse"])] = row["slope"]

# Prepare numpy arrays for vectorized computation
ach_arr = bge["ach50"].to_numpy().astype(float)
sqft_arr = bge["sqft"].to_numpy().astype(float)
w_arr = bge["weight"].to_numpy().astype(float)
group_arr = bge["group"].to_list()
total_kwh = bge["grid_cons_kwh"].to_numpy().astype(float)
heat_kwh = bge["elec_heating_kwh"].to_numpy().astype(float)
cool_kwh = bge["elec_cooling_kwh"].to_numpy().astype(float)
gas_heat_kwh = bge["gas_heating_kwh"].to_numpy().astype(float)
gas_total_kwh = bge["out.natural_gas.total.energy_consumption.kwh"].to_numpy().astype(float)
gas_other_kwh = gas_total_kwh - gas_heat_kwh
other_kwh = total_kwh - heat_kwh - cool_kwh

customer_scale = TEST_YEAR_CC / w_arr.sum()
original_total_gwh = (w_arr * total_kwh).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9
original_gas_gwh = (w_arr * gas_total_kwh).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9
test_year_gwh = TEST_YEAR_KWH / 1e9

sweep_results = []
for delta_pct in range(0, 55, 5):
    delta = delta_pct / 100.0

    corrected_heat = np.copy(heat_kwh)
    corrected_cool = np.copy(cool_kwh)
    corrected_gas_heat = np.copy(gas_heat_kwh)

    for i in range(len(bge)):
        g = group_arr[i]
        s_heat = slope_lookup.get((g, "Elec heating"), 0.0)
        s_cool = slope_lookup.get((g, "Elec cooling"), 0.0)
        s_gas = slope_lookup.get((g, "Gas heating"), 0.0)
        corrected_heat[i] = max(0, heat_kwh[i] - s_heat * sqft_arr[i] * ach_arr[i] * delta)
        corrected_cool[i] = max(0, cool_kwh[i] - s_cool * sqft_arr[i] * ach_arr[i] * delta)
        corrected_gas_heat[i] = max(0, gas_heat_kwh[i] - s_gas * sqft_arr[i] * ach_arr[i] * delta)

    corrected_total = corrected_heat + corrected_cool + other_kwh
    corrected_gas_total = corrected_gas_heat + gas_other_kwh
    corrected_gwh = (w_arr * corrected_total).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9
    corrected_gas_gwh = (w_arr * corrected_gas_total).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9

    sweep_results.append({
        "delta_pct": delta_pct,
        "corrected_elec_gwh": corrected_gwh,
        "corrected_gas_gwh": corrected_gas_gwh,
        "gap_to_test_year_pct": (corrected_gwh - test_year_gwh) / test_year_gwh * 100,
        "gas_change_pct": (corrected_gas_gwh - original_gas_gwh) / original_gas_gwh * 100,
    })

sweep_df = pl.DataFrame(sweep_results)
```

```{python}
#| label: show-sweep

sweep_df.with_columns(
    pl.col("corrected_elec_gwh").round(2),
    pl.col("corrected_gas_gwh").round(2),
    pl.col("gap_to_test_year_pct").round(1).alias("elec_gap_%"),
    pl.col("gas_change_pct").round(1).alias("gas_change_%"),
).select("delta_pct", "corrected_elec_gwh", "elec_gap_%", "corrected_gas_gwh", "gas_change_%")
```

```{python}
)

fig = p.draw()
display_figure(fig)
```

## LBNL ResDB benchmark: what should BGE's ACH50 distribution look like?

Rather than choosing an ACH50 correction to hit the test-year target, we derive the
correction from an independent, published source: the **LBNL Residential Diagnostics
Database regression model** (Chan, Joh & Sherman 2013, _Energy and Buildings_ 66: 616–625).

This model predicts normalized leakage (NL) — a dimensionless, size-adjusted air leakage
metric — from a home's vintage, climate zone, floor area, and height, based on 134,000
field blower-door measurements across 43 U.S. states. It explains 68% of observed variance
in NL. Crucially, **ResStock itself draws its ACH50 assignments from this same database**,
so using the published regression as a benchmark is internally consistent.

The key regression (Eq. 4 / Table 3 in Chan et al.):

$$\ln(\text{NL}) = \hat{\beta}_{\text{year}} + \hat{\beta}_{\text{cz}} + \hat{\beta}_{\text{area}} \times A + \hat{\beta}_h \times H$$

where $A$ is floor area (m²) and $H$ is building height (m). For typical homes that are
neither low-income weatherization participants nor energy-efficiency rated, the WAP and
energy-rating indicator terms are zero.

The approximate conversion is $\text{ACH50} \approx C \times \text{NL} / H^{0.7}$, where
$C \approx 39.3$ is calibrated from the paper's rule of thumb (NL = 0.55 ↔ ACH50 = 10
for a typical single-story home at H = 3 m).

```{python}
#| label: chan-regression

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Chan et al. (2013) Table 3 regression coefficients
# -----------------------------------------------------------------

# Year-built indicators (β_year)
BETA_YEAR = {
    "prior_1960": -0.250,
    "1960s": -0.433,
    "1970s": -0.452,
    "1980s": -0.654,
    "1990s": -0.915,
    "2000_after": -1.058,
}

# Climate zone: Maryland = IECC 4A (Humid-4)
BETA_CZ_4A = 0.326

# Continuous variables
BETA_AREA = -0.00208   # per m² of floor area
BETA_H = 0.0638        # per m of building height

# NL → ACH50 conversion constant (calibrated: NL=0.55 → ACH50=10 at H=3m)
C_NL_ACH50 = 39.3

def resstock_vintage_to_chan(vintage: str) -> str:
    """Map ResStock's in.vintage to Chan et al. vintage category."""
    if vintage in ("<1940", "1940s", "1950s"):
        return "prior_1960"
    elif vintage == "1960s":
        return "1960s"
    elif vintage == "1970s":
        return "1970s"
    elif vintage == "1980s":
        return "1980s"
    elif vintage == "1990s":
        return "1990s"
    else:  # 2000s, 2010s
        return "2000_after"

def stories_to_height_m(stories_str: str) -> float:
    """Convert ResStock stories to building height (m).

    Chan et al. convention: 3m for 1-story, 5.5m for 2-story, 8m for 3-story.
    For tall MF buildings, cap at 3 stories for the NL model (which was
    developed for single-family detached homes).
    """
    try:
        s = int(stories_str)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return 3.0
    s = min(s, 3)
    return 2.5 * s + 0.5

def predict_ach50_chan(vintage: str, sqft: float, stories: str) -> float:
    """Predict ACH50 for a single building using Chan et al. (2013)."""
    beta_yr = BETA_YEAR[resstock_vintage_to_chan(vintage)]
    area_m2 = sqft / 10.764
    h_m = stories_to_height_m(stories)

    ln_nl = beta_yr + BETA_CZ_4A + BETA_AREA * area_m2 + BETA_H * h_m
    nl = np.exp(ln_nl)
    return C_NL_ACH50 * nl / (h_m ** 0.7)

print("Chan et al. (2013) regression implemented.")
print(f"Climate zone: 4A (β_cz = {BETA_CZ_4A})")
print(f"WAP / energy-rated indicators: both 0 (typical housing stock)")
```

Now apply this per-building to the BGE ResStock sample:

```{python}
#| label: benchmark-comparison

vintage_arr = bge["in.vintage"].to_list()
stories_arr = bge["in.geometry_stories"].to_list()

predicted_ach50 = np.array([
    predict_ach50_chan(vintage_arr[i], sqft_arr[i], stories_arr[i])
    for i in range(len(bge))
])

wtd_mean_predicted = (predicted_ach50 * w_arr).sum() / w_arr.sum()
wtd_mean_resstock = (ach_arr * w_arr).sum() / w_arr.sum()

overshoot_ratio = wtd_mean_resstock / wtd_mean_predicted
delta_benchmark = 1.0 - 1.0 / overshoot_ratio

print(f"Chan et al. predicted weighted-mean ACH50:   {wtd_mean_predicted:.1f}")
print(f"ResStock assigned weighted-mean ACH50:       {wtd_mean_resstock:.1f}")
print(f"Overshoot ratio (ResStock / benchmark):      {overshoot_ratio:.2f}")
print(f"Implied uniform correction δ:                {delta_benchmark:.1%}")
print()
print(f"In other words, ResStock's ACH50 values for BGE homes are")
print(f"{(overshoot_ratio - 1) * 100:.0f}% higher than what the Chan et al. regression")
print(f"predicts for the same vintage, climate zone, and building size distribution.")
```

### Benchmark by vintage

The overshoot may vary by vintage — ResStock may be more accurate for newer homes
(where code compliance data is better) than for older ones:

```{python}
#| label: benchmark-by-vintage

bge_check = bge.with_columns(
    pl.Series("predicted_ach50", predicted_ach50),
)

vintage_comparison = (
    bge_check
    .group_by("in.vintage")
    .agg(
        (pl.col("ach50") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
        (pl.col("predicted_ach50") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
        pl.col("weight").sum().alias("total_weight"),
    )
    .rename({"ach50": "resstock_ach50", "predicted_ach50": "chan_ach50"})
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("resstock_ach50") / pl.col("chan_ach50")).alias("ratio"),
    )
    .sort("in.vintage")
)

vintage_comparison.with_columns(
    pl.col("resstock_ach50").round(1),
    pl.col("chan_ach50").round(1),
    pl.col("ratio").round(2),
)
```

## Apply the benchmark-driven correction

The Chan et al. regression gives us a defensible, per-building target ACH50 derived from
a published model based on 134,000 field measurements. The implied correction ratio tells
us by how much to uniformly reduce ACH50, then we propagate that through the heating/cooling
regressions fitted earlier in this notebook.

```{python}
#| label: solve-delta

# Per-building "correctable per unit delta": slope * sqft * ach50
correctable_heat = np.array([
    slope_lookup.get((group_arr[i], "Elec heating"), 0.0) * sqft_arr[i] * ach_arr[i]
    for i in range(len(bge))
])
correctable_cool = np.array([
    slope_lookup.get((group_arr[i], "Elec cooling"), 0.0) * sqft_arr[i] * ach_arr[i]
    for i in range(len(bge))
])
correctable_gas_heat = np.array([
    slope_lookup.get((group_arr[i], "Gas heating"), 0.0) * sqft_arr[i] * ach_arr[i]
    for i in range(len(bge))
])
elec_correctable_gwh = (w_arr * (correctable_heat + correctable_cool)).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9

# δ* that would fully close the electric gap (for reference only)
delta_star_full = (original_total_gwh - test_year_gwh) / elec_correctable_gwh

print(f"Original electric total:     {original_total_gwh:>10.2f} GWh")
print(f"Test-year target:            {test_year_gwh:>10.2f} GWh")
print(f"Gap:                         {original_total_gwh - test_year_gwh:>+10.2f} GWh ({(original_total_gwh - test_year_gwh) / test_year_gwh * 100:+.1f}%)")
print()
print(f"Benchmark-driven δ (Chan et al.):  {delta_benchmark:.1%}")
print(f"Gap-closing δ* (electric only):    {delta_star_full:.1%}")
print()
if delta_benchmark < delta_star_full:
    print(f"The benchmark correction ({delta_benchmark:.0%}) is smaller than the δ*")
    print(f"needed to fully close the gap ({delta_star_full:.0%}), meaning ACH50")
    print(f"overestimation alone does not explain all of the discrepancy.")
else:
    print(f"The benchmark correction ({delta_benchmark:.0%}) exceeds δ*")
    print(f"({delta_star_full:.0%}), suggesting ACH50 overestimation could")
    print(f"more than account for the total load gap.")
```

### Apply the correction

```{python}
#| label: apply-benchmark

corrected_heat_star = np.maximum(0, heat_kwh - delta_benchmark * correctable_heat)
corrected_cool_star = np.maximum(0, cool_kwh - delta_benchmark * correctable_cool)
corrected_gas_heat_star = np.maximum(0, gas_heat_kwh - delta_benchmark * correctable_gas_heat)
corrected_total_star = corrected_heat_star + corrected_cool_star + other_kwh
corrected_gas_total_star = corrected_gas_heat_star + gas_other_kwh

bge = bge.with_columns(
    pl.Series("corrected_heat_kwh", corrected_heat_star),
    pl.Series("corrected_cool_kwh", corrected_cool_star),
    pl.Series("corrected_gas_heat_kwh", corrected_gas_heat_star),
    pl.Series("corrected_total_kwh", corrected_total_star),
    pl.Series("corrected_gas_total_kwh", corrected_gas_total_star),
    pl.Series("predicted_ach50", predicted_ach50),
)

corrected_gwh_star = (w_arr * corrected_total_star).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9
corrected_gas_gwh_star = (w_arr * corrected_gas_total_star).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9
gap_closed_gwh = original_total_gwh - corrected_gwh_star
gap_total_gwh = original_total_gwh - test_year_gwh
pct_closed = gap_closed_gwh / gap_total_gwh * 100

corrected_mean_ach50 = wtd_mean_resstock * (1 - delta_benchmark)

print(f"Benchmark-driven correction: δ = {delta_benchmark:.1%}")
print(f"  ResStock mean ACH50:   {wtd_mean_resstock:.1f} → {corrected_mean_ach50:.1f}")
print(f"  Chan et al. target:    {wtd_mean_predicted:.1f}")
print()
print(f"ELECTRIC")
print(f"  Original total:        {original_total_gwh:.2f} GWh")
print(f"  Corrected total:       {corrected_gwh_star:.2f} GWh")
print(f"  Test-year target:      {test_year_gwh:.2f} GWh")
print(f"  Gap closed:            {gap_closed_gwh:.2f} GWh of {gap_total_gwh:.2f} GWh ({pct_closed:.0f}%)")
print(f"  Remaining gap:         {corrected_gwh_star - test_year_gwh:+.2f} GWh ({(corrected_gwh_star - test_year_gwh) / test_year_gwh * 100:+.1f}%)")
print()
gas_change_pct = (corrected_gas_gwh_star - original_gas_gwh) / original_gas_gwh * 100
print(f"NATURAL GAS")
print(f"  Original total:        {original_gas_gwh:.2f} GWh (thermal)")
print(f"  Corrected total:       {corrected_gas_gwh_star:.2f} GWh (thermal)")
print(f"  Change:                {gas_change_pct:+.1f}%")
```

## Group-level impact

How does the benchmark-driven correction distribute across heating-type groups? The
within-ResStock regression slopes differ by group and end-use (electric heating, electric
cooling, gas heating), so the same ACH50 correction produces group-specific load reductions.

```{python}
#| label: group-impact

for g in GROUPS:
    mask = np.array([x == g for x in group_arr])
    w_g = w_arr[mask]
    orig_g = (w_g * total_kwh[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()
    corr_g = (w_g * corrected_total_star[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()
    heat_orig = (w_g * heat_kwh[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()
    heat_corr = (w_g * corrected_heat_star[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()
    cool_orig = (w_g * cool_kwh[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()
    cool_corr = (w_g * corrected_cool_star[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()
    gas_orig = (w_g * gas_heat_kwh[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()
    gas_corr = (w_g * corrected_gas_heat_star[mask]).sum() / w_g.sum()

    print(f"{g}")
    print(f"  Elec total:    {orig_g:>10,.0f} → {corr_g:>10,.0f}  ({(corr_g - orig_g) / orig_g * 100:+.1f}%)")
    print(f"  Elec heating:  {heat_orig:>10,.0f} → {heat_corr:>10,.0f}  ({(heat_corr - heat_orig) / heat_orig * 100 if heat_orig > 0 else 0:+.1f}%)")
    print(f"  Elec cooling:  {cool_orig:>10,.0f} → {cool_corr:>10,.0f}  ({(cool_corr - cool_orig) / cool_orig * 100 if cool_orig > 0 else 0:+.1f}%)")
    if gas_orig > 0:
        print(f"  Gas heating:   {gas_orig:>10,.0f} → {gas_corr:>10,.0f}  ({(gas_corr - gas_orig) / gas_orig * 100:+.1f}%)")
    print()
```

## RECS comparison: how much of the kWh/sqft gap does ACH50 explain?

The RECS benchmarks computed above give us independent targets for each end-use and
heating-type group. We can compare the benchmark-driven regression correction to those
targets:

```{python}
#| label: recs-coverage

print(f"Benchmark-driven ACH50 correction: δ = {delta_benchmark:.1%}")
print()

# --- Gap-closing against original benchmarks (TOTSQFT_EN) ---
print("Against RECS benchmarks using total sqft (TOTSQFT_EN):")
print(f"{'Group':<15s}  {'End-use':<15s}  {'RS orig':>8s}  {'RS corr':>8s}  "
      f"{'RECS':>6s}  {'Gap closed':>10s}")
print(f"{'-'*15}  {'-'*15}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*6}  {'-'*10}")

for (g, eu), recs_val in RECS_BENCHMARKS.items():
    sub_mask = np.array([x == g for x in group_arr])
    w_g = w_arr[sub_mask]
    sqft_g = sqft_arr[sub_mask]

    if eu == "Elec heating":
        orig_vals = heat_kwh[sub_mask]
        corr_vals = corrected_heat_star[sub_mask]
    elif eu == "Elec cooling":
        orig_vals = cool_kwh[sub_mask]
        corr_vals = corrected_cool_star[sub_mask]
    elif eu == "Gas heating":
        orig_vals = gas_heat_kwh[sub_mask]
        corr_vals = corrected_gas_heat_star[sub_mask]
    else:
        continue

    orig_per_sqft = (w_g * orig_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    corr_per_sqft = (w_g * corr_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()

    original_gap = orig_per_sqft - recs_val
    closed = orig_per_sqft - corr_per_sqft
    pct_closed = closed / original_gap * 100 if original_gap > 0 else 0

    print(f"{g:<15s}  {eu:<15s}  {orig_per_sqft:>8.2f}  {corr_per_sqft:>8.2f}  "
          f"{recs_val:>6.2f}  {pct_closed:>9.0f}%")

# --- Gap-closing against adjusted benchmarks (conditioned sqft) ---
# ResStock divides by total sqft (it assumes whole-house conditioning),
# so the "gap" to the adjusted RECS benchmark (which uses conditioned sqft)
# is smaller — the adjusted benchmark is higher, closer to ResStock.
print()
print("Against RECS benchmarks using conditioned sqft (TOTHSQFT / TOTCSQFT):")
print(f"{'Group':<15s}  {'End-use':<15s}  {'RS orig':>8s}  {'RS corr':>8s}  "
      f"{'RECS adj':>8s}  {'Gap closed':>10s}")
print(f"{'-'*15}  {'-'*15}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*10}")

for (g, eu), recs_adj in RECS_BENCHMARKS_ADJUSTED.items():
    sub_mask = np.array([x == g for x in group_arr])
    w_g = w_arr[sub_mask]
    sqft_g = sqft_arr[sub_mask]

    if eu == "Elec heating":
        orig_vals = heat_kwh[sub_mask]
        corr_vals = corrected_heat_star[sub_mask]
    elif eu == "Elec cooling":
        orig_vals = cool_kwh[sub_mask]
        corr_vals = corrected_cool_star[sub_mask]
    elif eu == "Gas heating":
        orig_vals = gas_heat_kwh[sub_mask]
        corr_vals = corrected_gas_heat_star[sub_mask]
    else:
        continue

    # ResStock still uses total sqft (whole-house assumption)
    orig_per_sqft = (w_g * orig_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    corr_per_sqft = (w_g * corr_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()

    adj_gap = orig_per_sqft - recs_adj
    closed = orig_per_sqft - corr_per_sqft
    pct_closed = closed / adj_gap * 100 if adj_gap > 0 else 0

    print(f"{g:<15s}  {eu:<15s}  {orig_per_sqft:>8.2f}  {corr_per_sqft:>8.2f}  "
          f"{recs_adj:>8.2f}  {pct_closed:>9.0f}%")

print()
print("The adjusted RECS benchmarks are higher (more kWh per conditioned sqft),")
print("so the original gap is smaller and the ACH50 correction closes a larger")
print("fraction of it. This makes sense: part of the ResStock-vs-RECS gap was")
print("never about infiltration — it was about ResStock conditioning the whole")
print("house while real homes condition only a portion.")
```

## Per-building ACH50 correction

The uniform correction above applies a single δ = `{python} f"{delta_benchmark:.1%}"` to
every home, derived from the ratio of weighted means. But the Chan et al. regression already
gives us a per-building ACH50 prediction — conditioned on each home's vintage, floor area,
and height — so we can target the correction where the discrepancy actually is.

The per-building correction uses each home's own Chan-predicted ACH50 as the target:

$$\text{kWh}'_i = \max\!\Big(0,\; \text{kWh}_i - b_{g,e} \times \text{sqft}_i \times \big(\text{ACH50}^{\text{RS}}_i - \text{ACH50}^{\text{Chan}}_i\big)\Big)$$

This is still a correction, not a replacement: the original ResStock-simulated load (which
encodes thermostat settings, occupancy, equipment, shell quality, duct losses, and everything
else) is the starting point. Only the infiltration component changes, by the amount implied
by the per-building ACH50 discrepancy. Homes where ResStock and Chan agree get little or no
correction; homes where ResStock substantially overshoots get a larger correction.

Note that for some buildings, Chan may predict a _higher_ ACH50 than ResStock assigned. In
those cases, the correction increases the load — the formula is symmetric. This is physically
consistent: if a building was assigned a too-tight envelope, its simulated infiltration loss
was too low.

```{python}
#| label: per-building-correction

# Per-building ΔACH50: positive means ResStock overestimates (correction reduces load)
delta_ach50_per_bldg = ach_arr - predicted_ach50

# Per-building corrected end-use loads
pb_heat = np.array([
    max(0, heat_kwh[i] - slope_lookup.get((group_arr[i], "Elec heating"), 0.0)
        * sqft_arr[i] * delta_ach50_per_bldg[i])
    for i in range(len(bge))
])
pb_cool = np.array([
    max(0, cool_kwh[i] - slope_lookup.get((group_arr[i], "Elec cooling"), 0.0)
        * sqft_arr[i] * delta_ach50_per_bldg[i])
    for i in range(len(bge))
])
pb_gas_heat = np.array([
    max(0, gas_heat_kwh[i] - slope_lookup.get((group_arr[i], "Gas heating"), 0.0)
        * sqft_arr[i] * delta_ach50_per_bldg[i])
    for i in range(len(bge))
])

pb_total = pb_heat + pb_cool + other_kwh
pb_gas_total = pb_gas_heat + gas_other_kwh

# Attach to the DataFrame for downstream analysis
bge = bge.with_columns(
    pl.Series("pb_corrected_heat_kwh", pb_heat),
    pl.Series("pb_corrected_cool_kwh", pb_cool),
    pl.Series("pb_corrected_gas_heat_kwh", pb_gas_heat),
    pl.Series("pb_corrected_total_kwh", pb_total),
    pl.Series("pb_corrected_gas_total_kwh", pb_gas_total),
    pl.Series("delta_ach50", delta_ach50_per_bldg),
)

pb_elec_gwh = (w_arr * pb_total).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9
pb_gas_gwh = (w_arr * pb_gas_total).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9

print("Per-building ACH50 correction applied.")
print(f"  Buildings with ΔACH50 > 0 (load reduced):   {(delta_ach50_per_bldg > 0).sum():,}")
print(f"  Buildings with ΔACH50 ≈ 0 (unchanged):      {(np.abs(delta_ach50_per_bldg) < 0.5).sum():,}")
print(f"  Buildings with ΔACH50 < 0 (load increased):  {(delta_ach50_per_bldg < 0).sum():,}")
```

### Vintage-level correction scale

The per-building approach applies different effective δ values to different vintages, because
the Chan et al. overshoot is not uniform across the housing stock. Older homes see larger
absolute corrections; newer homes (where ResStock is closer to the benchmark) see smaller
ones.

```{python}
#| label: pb-vintage-delta

pb_vintage = (
    bge.select("in.vintage", "ach50", "predicted_ach50", "delta_ach50", "weight")
    .group_by("in.vintage")
    .agg(
        (pl.col("ach50") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
        (pl.col("predicted_ach50") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
        (pl.col("delta_ach50") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
        pl.col("weight").sum().alias("total_weight"),
        pl.len().alias("n"),
    )
    .rename({"ach50": "rs_mean_ach50", "predicted_ach50": "chan_mean_ach50",
             "delta_ach50": "mean_delta_ach50"})
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("rs_mean_ach50") / pl.col("chan_mean_ach50")).alias("overshoot_ratio"),
        (1 - pl.col("chan_mean_ach50") / pl.col("rs_mean_ach50")).alias("effective_delta"),
    )
    .sort("in.vintage")
)

pb_vintage.select(
    "in.vintage",
    pl.col("rs_mean_ach50").round(1),
    pl.col("chan_mean_ach50").round(1),
    pl.col("mean_delta_ach50").round(1),
    pl.col("overshoot_ratio").round(2),
    (pl.col("effective_delta") * 100).round(1).alias("effective_δ_%"),
    "n",
)
```

For comparison, the uniform approach applies δ = `{python} f"{delta_benchmark:.1%}"` to
every vintage. The per-building approach lets each vintage settle at its own effective
correction.

## Fitted-ratio correction

The per-building formula above subtracts a **population-average kWh voucher**
($b \times \text{sqft} \times \Delta\text{ACH50}$) from this house's actual load, then
floors at zero. That voucher is what the regression says a house of this size and leakiness
_should_ save. Houses that already sit far below the fitted line — typically low-intensity
multifamily units — have a smaller bill than the voucher, so the floor fires and heating
goes to zero.

On the fitted line the two operations are the same. A house with
$\text{kWh} = (a + b \cdot \text{ACH50}) \times \text{sqft}$ loses exactly
$b \times \text{sqft} \times \Delta$ kWh, which is also a multiplicative scale by
$(a + b \cdot \text{ACH50}^{\text{Chan}}) / (a + b \cdot \text{ACH50}^{\text{RS}})$.
Off the line they diverge. The **fitted-ratio** method always applies that multiplicative
scale, using the intercept $a$ as well as the slope $b$:

$$\text{kWh}'_i = \text{kWh}_i \times \frac{a_{g,e} + b_{g,e} \cdot \text{ACH50}^{\text{Chan}}_i}{a_{g,e} + b_{g,e} \cdot \text{ACH50}^{\text{RS}}_i}$$

Same per-building $\Delta\text{ACH50}$ as the subtractive method. Every house with the same
ACH50 in the same group gets the same fraction, whether it used 1,700 kWh or 9,500. The
ratio cannot exceed a 100% cut as long as $a + b \cdot \text{ACH50}^{\text{RS}} > 0$.

```{python}
#| label: fitted-ratio-correction

intercept_lookup: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}
for row in reg_df.iter_rows(named=True):
    intercept_lookup[(row["group"], row["enduse"])] = row["intercept"]


def _fitted_ratio_scale(
    orig: np.ndarray,
    enduse: str,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Scale each building's load by ê(Chan) / ê(ResStock) from the fitted line."""
    out = np.copy(orig)
    for i in range(len(orig)):
        key = (group_arr[i], enduse)
        a = intercept_lookup.get(key, 0.0)
        b = slope_lookup.get(key, 0.0)
        pred_old = a + b * ach_arr[i]
        pred_new = a + b * predicted_ach50[i]
        if pred_old > 1e-9:
            out[i] = orig[i] * max(pred_new / pred_old, 0.0)
    return out


ratio_heat = _fitted_ratio_scale(heat_kwh, "Elec heating")
ratio_cool = _fitted_ratio_scale(cool_kwh, "Elec cooling")
ratio_gas_heat = _fitted_ratio_scale(gas_heat_kwh, "Gas heating")
ratio_total = ratio_heat + ratio_cool + other_kwh
ratio_gas_total = ratio_gas_heat + gas_other_kwh

bge = bge.with_columns(
    pl.Series("ratio_corrected_heat_kwh", ratio_heat),
    pl.Series("ratio_corrected_cool_kwh", ratio_cool),
    pl.Series("ratio_corrected_gas_heat_kwh", ratio_gas_heat),
    pl.Series("ratio_corrected_total_kwh", ratio_total),
    pl.Series("ratio_corrected_gas_total_kwh", ratio_gas_total),
)

ratio_elec_gwh = (w_arr * ratio_total).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9
ratio_gas_gwh = (w_arr * ratio_gas_total).sum() * customer_scale / 1e9

n_heat_zero_sub = int(((heat_kwh > 1) & (pb_heat <= 1e-9)).sum())
n_heat_zero_ratio = int(((heat_kwh > 1) & (ratio_heat <= 1e-9)).sum())
n_cool_zero_sub = int(((cool_kwh > 1) & (pb_cool <= 1e-9)).sum())
n_cool_zero_ratio = int(((cool_kwh > 1) & (ratio_cool <= 1e-9)).sum())
n_gas_zero_sub = int(((gas_heat_kwh > 1) & (pb_gas_heat <= 1e-9)).sum())
n_gas_zero_ratio = int(((gas_heat_kwh > 1) & (ratio_gas_heat <= 1e-9)).sum())

# Effective frac on heating (1 - kWh'/kWh), among homes with heating
heat_pos = heat_kwh > 1
sub_frac = np.where(heat_pos, 1 - pb_heat / heat_kwh, np.nan)
ratio_frac = np.where(heat_pos, 1 - ratio_heat / heat_kwh, np.nan)


def _wtd_pct(arr: np.ndarray, q: float) -> float:
    m = np.isfinite(arr)
    order = np.argsort(arr[m])
    cw = np.cumsum(w_arr[m][order])
    cw = cw / cw[-1]
    return float(arr[m][order][np.searchsorted(cw, q, side="left")])


print("Fitted-ratio correction applied (same per-building ΔACH50 as subtract).")
print()
print("Homes with original load > 1 kWh driven to ~0:")
print(f"  {'':16s}  {'Subtract':>10s}  {'Fit-ratio':>10s}")
print(f"  {'Elec heating':16s}  {n_heat_zero_sub:>10,d}  {n_heat_zero_ratio:>10,d}")
print(f"  {'Elec cooling':16s}  {n_cool_zero_sub:>10,d}  {n_cool_zero_ratio:>10,d}")
print(f"  {'Gas heating':16s}  {n_gas_zero_sub:>10,d}  {n_gas_zero_ratio:>10,d}")
print()
print("Electric heating frac (1 − kWh'/kWh), homes with heating:")
print(f"  {'':16s}  {'Subtract':>10s}  {'Fit-ratio':>10s}")
print(f"  {'median':16s}  {_wtd_pct(sub_frac, 0.50):>10.2f}  {_wtd_pct(ratio_frac, 0.50):>10.2f}")
print(f"  {'p90':16s}  {_wtd_pct(sub_frac, 0.90):>10.2f}  {_wtd_pct(ratio_frac, 0.90):>10.2f}")
print(f"  {'p99':16s}  {_wtd_pct(sub_frac, 0.99):>10.2f}  {_wtd_pct(ratio_frac, 0.99):>10.2f}")
print(f"  {'max':16s}  {np.nanmax(sub_frac):>10.2f}  {np.nanmax(ratio_frac):>10.2f}")
```

On the line, subtract and fitted-ratio agree. Off the line, subtract takes a larger bite
from low-intensity homes (to the point of deleting heating) and a smaller bite from
high-intensity homes. Fitted-ratio keeps the typical home's correction nearly unchanged
and only rewrites that tail.

```{python}
for g in GROUPS:
    mask = np.array([x == g for x in group_arr])
    w_g = w_arr[mask]

    for label, orig, uniform_corr, pb_corr, ratio_corr in [
        ("Elec total",   total_kwh[mask],    corrected_total_star[mask],     pb_total[mask],     ratio_total[mask]),
        ("Elec heating",  heat_kwh[mask],     corrected_heat_star[mask],      pb_heat[mask],      ratio_heat[mask]),
        ("Elec cooling",  cool_kwh[mask],     corrected_cool_star[mask],      pb_cool[mask],      ratio_cool[mask]),
        ("Gas heating",   gas_heat_kwh[mask], corrected_gas_heat_star[mask],  pb_gas_heat[mask],  ratio_gas_heat[mask]),
    ]:
        orig_avg = (w_g * orig).sum() / w_g.sum()
        if orig_avg < 1:
            continue
        uni_avg = (w_g * uniform_corr).sum() / w_g.sum()

        ratio_avg = (w_g * ratio_corr).sum() / w_g.sum()

        print(f"{g:<15s}  {label:<15s}  {orig_avg:>10,.0f}  {uni_avg:>10,.0f}  "
              f"{pb_avg:>10,.0f}  {ratio_avg:>10,.0f}  "
              f"{(uni_avg - orig_avg) / orig_avg * 100:>+7.1f}%  "
              f"{(pb_avg - orig_avg) / orig_avg * 100:>+7.1f}%  "
              f"{(ratio_avg - orig_avg) / orig_avg * 100:>+7.1f}%")
```

### RECS kWh/sqft comparison

How close do the three corrections get to the independent RECS benchmarks?

```{python}
#| label: pb-recs-comparison

def _enduse_vals(eu: str, sub_mask: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    if eu == "Elec heating":
        return (
            heat_kwh[sub_mask],
            corrected_heat_star[sub_mask],
            pb_heat[sub_mask],
            ratio_heat[sub_mask],
        )
    if eu == "Elec cooling":
        return (
            cool_kwh[sub_mask],
            corrected_cool_star[sub_mask],
            pb_cool[sub_mask],
            ratio_cool[sub_mask],
        )
    if eu == "Gas heating":
        return (
            gas_heat_kwh[sub_mask],
            corrected_gas_heat_star[sub_mask],
            pb_gas_heat[sub_mask],
            ratio_gas_heat[sub_mask],
        )
    raise ValueError(eu)


def _gap_closed(orig_psf: float, new_psf: float, recs: float) -> float:
    gap = orig_psf - recs
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return (orig_psf - new_psf) / gap * 100


# --- Against original benchmarks (total sqft) ---
print("Against RECS benchmarks using total sqft (TOTSQFT_EN):")
print(f"{'Group':<15s}  {'End-use':<15s}  {'RS orig':>8s}  {'Uniform':>8s}  "
      f"{'Subtract':>8s}  {'Fit-ratio':>9s}  {'RECS':>6s}  "
      f"{'Unif':>6s}  {'Sub':>6s}  {'Ratio':>6s}")
print(f"{'-'*15}  {'-'*15}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*9}  {'-'*6}  "
      f"{'-'*6}  {'-'*6}  {'-'*6}")

for (g, eu), recs_val in RECS_BENCHMARKS.items():
    sub_mask = np.array([x == g for x in group_arr])
    w_g = w_arr[sub_mask]
    sqft_g = sqft_arr[sub_mask]
    orig_vals, uni_vals, pb_vals, ratio_vals = _enduse_vals(eu, sub_mask)

    orig_psf = (w_g * orig_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    uni_psf = (w_g * uni_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    pb_psf = (w_g * pb_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    ratio_psf = (w_g * ratio_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()

    print(f"{g:<15s}  {eu:<15s}  {orig_psf:>8.2f}  {uni_psf:>8.2f}  "
          f"{pb_psf:>8.2f}  {ratio_psf:>9.2f}  {recs_val:>6.2f}  "
          f"{_gap_closed(orig_psf, uni_psf, recs_val):>5.0f}%  "
          f"{_gap_closed(orig_psf, pb_psf, recs_val):>5.0f}%  "
          f"{_gap_closed(orig_psf, ratio_psf, recs_val):>5.0f}%")

# --- Against adjusted benchmarks (conditioned sqft) ---
print()
print("Against RECS benchmarks using conditioned sqft (TOTHSQFT / TOTCSQFT):")
print(f"{'Group':<15s}  {'End-use':<15s}  {'RS orig':>8s}  {'Uniform':>8s}  "
      f"{'Subtract':>8s}  {'Fit-ratio':>9s}  {'RECS adj':>8s}  "
      f"{'Unif':>6s}  {'Sub':>6s}  {'Ratio':>6s}")
print(f"{'-'*15}  {'-'*15}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*8}  {'-'*9}  {'-'*8}  "
      f"{'-'*6}  {'-'*6}  {'-'*6}")

for (g, eu), recs_adj in RECS_BENCHMARKS_ADJUSTED.items():
    sub_mask = np.array([x == g for x in group_arr])
    w_g = w_arr[sub_mask]
    sqft_g = sqft_arr[sub_mask]
    orig_vals, uni_vals, pb_vals, ratio_vals = _enduse_vals(eu, sub_mask)

    orig_psf = (w_g * orig_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    uni_psf = (w_g * uni_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    pb_psf = (w_g * pb_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()
    ratio_psf = (w_g * ratio_vals / sqft_g).sum() / w_g.sum()

    print(f"{g:<15s}  {eu:<15s}  {orig_psf:>8.2f}  {uni_psf:>8.2f}  "
          f"{pb_psf:>8.2f}  {ratio_psf:>9.2f}  {recs_adj:>8.2f}  "
          f"{_gap_closed(orig_psf, uni_psf, recs_adj):>5.0f}%  "
          f"{_gap_closed(orig_psf, pb_psf, recs_adj):>5.0f}%  "
          f"{_gap_closed(orig_psf, ratio_psf, recs_adj):>5.0f}%")
```
